resources.string: Start listening to position the stethoscope and hear the patient in real time, then record.
Tap Start Listening to preview the sound.
No stethoscope detected — will record from the phone\'s microphone
Tap the chest to mark the site. Optional, but the same heart looks different at each position — a report without it cannot be repeated.
4th intercostal space, lower left sternal border
Lies beneath the left breast: gently lift or move the breast aside and place the chest piece directly on the chest wall.
Each stretch of the recording is shaded by the phase the algorithm assigned it. Pinch to zoom, drag to scroll once zoomed, tap to read the phase at that moment.
The segmented plot could not be drawn for this recording.
The algorithm locates S1, systole, S2 and diastole, and screens for a murmur. It looks for that one finding only and does not replace a clinical assessment.
Too few clear heartbeats to judge. Reposition the stethoscope, keep still, and record again.
Development model: in cross-validated testing it caught %1$d%% of murmurs and cleared %2$d%% of recordings without one. \"No murmur detected\" does not rule a murmur out.
Development model with no reported accuracy. \"No murmur detected\" does not rule a murmur out.
Rhythm: too few clear beats to judge
The heart sounds could not be picked out clearly. Reposition the stethoscope, keep still, and record again.
Screening aid only. This analysis measures heart rate and rhythm regularity from the heart sounds. It does not detect murmurs or other abnormalities.
WhatsApp isn\'t installed — this opens the normal share sheet instead.
Keep this screen open. Recordings not analyzed yet are analyzed first, about 15 seconds each.
Saved %1$d recordings, with a recordings.csv index, to the folder %2$s.
Higher rates capture more detail but produce larger files. Confirm the required value with the algorithm team.
Which channel to keep when the stethoscope hardware sends two. Recordings are always saved as mono.
Shows exactly what the phone sees on the USB port. Open this with the stethoscope plugged in.
Adds an engineering scope: the phonocardiogram with real time and frequency axes, zoomable, so filter cutoffs can be measured rather than assumed. For bench work, not for patients.
This phone could not play the recording (%1$s). It is still saved and can be analyzed.

Plug the stethoscope into the phone\'s USB-C port and allow access when Android asks. The status card on the main screen shows when it is ready. Without it, the app records from the phone\'s microphone.
Enter the patient\'s details if you have them, then tap Start Listening. Move the stethoscope until the heartbeat shows clearly on the live waveform.
Tap Record and keep the stethoscope still. Recording stops by itself when the time is up, or tap Stop to end early.
Tap the chest diagram to mark where you recorded, and play the clip back. Tap Analyze if it sounds clean, or Retake if not.

The analysis splits each heartbeat into S1, systole, S2 and diastole, and screens for a murmur. Tap Send via WhatsApp to send the report and audio to a doctor. Past recordings are in the Library (folder icon).

Raw capture is exactly what the app hands the algorithm: 16 kHz, unprocessed. PCG (2 kHz) previews the first step of the current placeholder algorithm, which decimates to 2 kHz itself. Pick a stage below, pinch the plots to zoom, tap to measure. Chain response is the one true gain measurement; the analog front end cannot be characterised from a recording.
Capture a few seconds, or load the last recording, to see the traces.
Requesting %1$d Hz — the USB stethoscope reports its own rate, the microphone may substitute one.
Captured at %1$d Hz, not the %2$d Hz the hardware is specified for. The algorithm receives this rate as-is; the preview decimation still runs correctly, but the ratio is no longer an exact ÷8.
Showing the first 20 s of a %1$d s recording.
dB is relative to the loudest bin in this trace, so compare shapes, not absolute levels. For an actual gain measurement, use the Chain response chip.

The one real gain measurement here: the PCG spectrum divided by the raw one, from the same clip, so everything except the resampling cancels out. That resampling now belongs to the placeholder algorithm, not the app — the app itself changes nothing. The dashed line is flat 0 dB and the solid line should sit on it; sag approaching 1 kHz is the anti-alias filter the decimation requires.
This measures the placeholder algorithm\'s decimation only. The analog front end and the acoustic coupling cannot be characterised from a recording — that needs a known input signal.
No response to show: this needs both the raw capture and the decimated output.

No voltage to show. These samples came from the phone\'s microphone, which has no defined voltage behind it — only a USB capture from the board can be read in volts, because its (raw − 2048) « 4 conversion is exact.

Absolute potential at the ADC pin, against the supply rails. The axis is fixed at the full rail on purpose: auto-ranging would make a 40 mV signal fill the plot and look healthy. No pass/fail band is drawn — nobody has measured yet what a real chest produces through this front end.
%1$d samples are sitting on a rail. The front end is clipping, and nothing downstream scales the signal back — this reaches the algorithm as a flattened peak.
Bias is %1$d mV off mid-rail. An off-centre bias loses swing to one rail before the other, so the signal clips earlier than the numbers suggest.
Swing is only %1$.1f%% of the rail. The RP2040\'s ADC is worth about 9 effective bits, so a signal this small is being digitised with very few usable levels — raise the preamp gain.
Firmware is not checked automatically. Tap Refresh to read its version, or Upload firmware to install the bundled version.
Board firmware is %1$s; this app bundles %2$s. Upload it from Settings → Hardware diagnostics.
Waiting for the firmware check to finish…
Plug the stethoscope in, then tap Refresh. Share this report with whoever is building the hardware — it says whether the phone sees a USB audio device, a serial device, or nothing at all.
A stethoscope is connected but Android has not granted this app access to it yet.
